articles.title: How Linux Handles a `fork()` When the Parent Has Gigabytes of Memory
articles.excerpt: A process with 8 GB of resident memory calls fork(). On a modern Linux system, the call returns in a few milliseconds. No 8 GB copy was made. The child is running. But something happened. The kernel d…
articles.body: A process with 8 GB of resident memory calls fork() . On a modern Linux system, the call returns in a few milliseconds. No 8 GB copy was made. The child is running. But something happened. The kernel did real work, and more real work is coming. Where did the cost go? What fork() Actually Creates fork() creates a new process with its own process ID, its own file descriptor table, its own signal state, and critically its own virtual address space. The child's address space is initially identical to the parent's: same virtual address ranges, same mappings, same content. What it does not have is its own copy of every physical memory page the parent mapped. The two processes share the underlying physical pages.

articles.title: A 24-second template beats infinite control (for a first version)
articles.excerpt: Every AI video tool starts with a control panel. Mine started with a fixed template, and that was the only reason it shipped. When the first version exposes duration, motion, style, aspect ratio and s…
articles.body: Every AI video tool starts with a control panel. Mine started with a fixed template, and that was the only reason it shipped. Infinite control is a trap for a first release When the first version exposes duration, motion, style, aspect ratio and seed, you are not giving the user power — you are giving them decisions they cannot evaluate. Users cannot tell a good seed from a bad one. They can tell whether the result looks right. A fixed template makes the first release testable: one input, one output shape, one thing to judge. 24 seconds is a constraint that clarifies A short fixed length forces three decisions: What has to happen in the first two seconds. Without a hook, nothing after it matters. What the loop point is.

articles.body: Most AWS security incidents do not start with an exotic exploit. They start with an over-broad policy, a key that was never rotated or a role that trusts more than it should, each created because it was the fastest way to make something work. Here are the IAM mistakes that recur most often, what to do instead, and how to check that the fix held. 1. Wildcards in actions and resources { "Effect" : "Allow" , "Action" : "*" , "Resource" : "*" } That is administrator access. Less obvious variants are s3:* on every bucket, or ec2:* for a pipeline that only starts and stops instances.

articles.body: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know. When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars? Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky. The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower.

articles.excerpt: Using data from the James Webb Space Telescope, astronomers have unravelled some of the secrets of a bizarre, blisteringly hot exoplanet that has the consistency of marshmallow.
articles.body: Using data from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers have unraveled some of the atmospheric secrets of a bizarre, blisteringly hot world that has the consistency of marshmallow. The extrasolar planet, or exoplanet , under the watchful infrared eye of the JWST , is WASP-17b, located around 1,300 light-years away. The exoplanet has a mass around 0.8 times that of Jupiter, but it is around twice as wide as the solar system's largest planet, giving it a "super-puff" consistency comparable to the Earth-based treat. WASP-17 b is so close to its parent star that it completes an orbit in under four Earth days, with this proximity also making the temperature of this " hot Jupiter " skyrocket.

articles.title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower 2026 peak this week — and when to look
articles.excerpt: The Orionids peak around Oct. 21. Here's when and where to look for the best chance of spotting meteors.
articles.body: If you love watching meteors, 2026 has given you plenty to enjoy. This summer, the annual Perseid meteor shower peaked on the day of a new moon — and a solar eclipse — so moonlight stayed out of the way. And there's more to look forward to: in December, the Geminids, the year's most prolific shower, will peak after a waxing crescent moon sets early in the evening, opening the door to excellent viewing. Right between those two headline showers, the dependable Orionids take their turn, reaching peak activity around Oct. 21-22. So, when and where can you catch the show? When and where to watch Make sure you wrap up warm for a night of Orionid hunting.

articles.title: SpaceX thrusters just made a Tesla Roadster 'fly' (and Elon Musk's car is still out there in space)
articles.excerpt: Tesla just unveiled its new Roadster with a spectacular stunt, using SpaceX thrusters to make the sleek vehicle "fly."
articles.body: Well, that was a memorable debut. Tesla unveiled its highly anticipated new Roadster last night (Oct. 16) with a spectacular stunt, using SpaceX thrusters to make the vehicle "fly." "This is not necessarily a safety-optimized car, OK?" Elon Musk , who runs both companies, said during the livestreamed reveal, which was held at SpaceX's rocket-testing facility in McGregor, Texas. "But it takes the the fun meter to 11 out of 10." Tesla's next-gen, thruster-equipped Roadster launches itself over other vehicles during an unveiling event on Oct. 15, 2026. (Image credit: Tesla) Tesla first announced the next-gen Roadster in 2017, saying at the time that it would be released in 2020 . In 2018, Musk announced that the new car would incorporate some SpaceX tech.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 16, 1975: NASA launches the 1st-ever GOES weather satellite to watch Earth from space
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 16, 1975, NASA launched the first operational GOES weather satellite. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 16, 1975, NASA launched the first operational GOES satellite! GOES-A was the first in a series of weather satellites that NASA jointly operated with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). The name is short for Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite . GOES-A launched on a Delta rocket from Cape Canaveral, Florida. GOES satellites all have a geostationary orbit, which means they always face the same part of Earth — in this case, the Indian Ocean. Once GOES-A became operational, it was renamed GOES-1. The GOES satellite fleet has grown over the years, and is a critical link in the chain of satellites tracking Earth's weather from space.
